urgent.title: First, a safety check

urgent.fainting: Fainting, or feeling like you will faint
urgent.highSugar: Very high blood sugar signs: extreme thirst, passing a lot of urine, confusion or very sleepy
urgent.goNowBody: These symptoms can be serious and need care today. Go to the nearest hospital now, or ask someone to take you. Do not drive yourself.
urgent.continue: I am safe, continue the risk check

risk.title: Risk check

sex.q: Are you a man or a woman?

age.help: This check is for adults 18 and older.

height.help: If you don't know, stand against a wall, mark the top of your head, and measure from the floor.

weight.help: Use a scale at home, a pharmacy or a health centre.

waist.help: Use a string: wrap it around your belly at the level of your belly button, breathe out normally, mark the string, then measure it with a ruler or tape. You can also use your trouser waist size as a rough guide.

activity.q: Do you do at least 30 minutes of physical activity every day?
activity.help: This includes physical work, walking, cycling, farming or exercise.

vegFruit.q: Do you eat vegetables or fruit every day?

bpMeds.q: Have you ever taken medicine for high blood pressure?

highGlucose.q: Has a health worker ever told you that your blood sugar was high?
highGlucose.help: For example at a check-up, while you were sick, or during pregnancy.

family.q: Has anyone in your family had diabetes?
family.second: Yes: grandparent, aunt, uncle or cousin
family.first: Yes: parent, brother, sister or my own child

smoker.help: Cigarettes, hand-rolled tobacco or other smoked tobacco.

sbp.q: Do you know your blood pressure?
sbp.help: Blood pressure is written like 130/80. Enter the top (bigger) number from a recent measurement.

province.q: Which province do you live in?
province.help: Optional. Used only for anonymous statistics.

about.title: About SokhaPheap
about.body: SokhaPheap helps adults in Cambodia understand their risk of type 2 diabetes and heart disease early, explains blood test results in simple language, and shows the nearest health facilities using Cambodian open data. It was built for the Open Data × AI Venture Hackathon, Phnom Penh, 2026.
about.how1: Diabetes risk uses the FINDRISC questionnaire (Finnish Diabetes Risk Score).
about.how2: Heart risk uses the WHO 2019 non-laboratory cardiovascular risk chart for South-East Asia.
about.how3: Scores are calculated by fixed rules, not by AI. AI is only used to read lab report photos and to explain results in simple words.
about.limit1: These scores were developed outside Cambodia and have not been validated in Cambodia yet.
about.limit2: Part of the facility data is from 2010. Some facilities may have moved, closed or changed.
about.limit3: Lab normal ranges vary between laboratories. We use the range printed on your report when there is one.
about.privacy: We do not ask for or store your name, phone number or ID. Lab photos are deleted right after reading. Risk results are saved without any personal details, for anonymous statistics.

method.title: How the Screening Gap Index works
method.p1: We combine five parts, each scored from 0 (smallest gap) to 1 (biggest gap) across all districts:
method.risk: Risk factors: women overweight or obese, men and women who smoke (DHS 2021–22, province level).
method.access: Distance to care: average travel time by car or motorbike, people more than an hour's walk from care (Malaria Atlas Project 2019 with WorldPop 2025), and women who say distance is a problem (DHS).
method.capacity: Few facilities: health facilities per 10,000 people (Ministry of Health 2010 and OpenStreetMap 2026, with WorldPop 2025).
method.people: Many adults: estimated adults aged 20+ (WorldPop 2025 and official 2024 age structure).
method.poverty: Poverty: people in the poorest fifth of households (DHS 2021–22).
method.p2: Each number is capped at the 5th and 95th percentile and scaled from 0 to 1. The five parts have equal weight. The index is their average × 100, so it runs from 0 to 100. The three parts that add the most are shown as the main reasons.
method.l1: Survey figures exist only per province, so all districts in a province share them, and they cover ages 15–49 only.
method.l2: Travel times are modelled for 2019 and may be different today. Facility data is partly from 2010.
method.l3: There is no province-level data on blood pressure or blood sugar, so these are not in the index.
method.l4: Changing the method changes the ranking. Our sensitivity check keeps 8 of the top 10 districts in a typical variation.
